items.summary: The Office of the Commissioner of Baseball and Public Broadcasting Service appealed a Copyright Royalty Board determination allocating 2014-2017 cable retransmission royalties among six competing claimant groups. The Board evaluated two valuation methodologies—regression analysis and constant-sum surveys—and concluded they should be equally weighted in calculating the relative marketplace value of competing programming categories. The Court of Appeals rejected nearly all of the appellants' challenges but vacated the determination and remanded, finding that while the Board's evaluation of the two methodologies was reasonable, the Board failed to explain how it merged those results to calculate the final allocation percentages among each claimant group.

items.summary: Lydia Bultemeyer filed a class action suit against CenturyLink under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, alleging the company unlawfully pulled her credit report after she completed step four of a five-step online ordering process but before she submitted her order at step five. CenturyLink asserted a Safeco defense, arguing that even if its interpretation of "initiated" a business transaction was erroneous, it was not objectively unreasonable and therefore not willful. The Ninth Circuit reversed the jury verdict of $28 million in statutory damages and $112 million in punitive damages, holding that CenturyLink was entitled to judgment as a matter of law because its reading of the Fair Credit Reporting Act had foundation in the statutory text and no court of appeals or authoritative guidance had warned against that construction.

items.summary: Steven Hecke, a federal prisoner, sued Sergeant Jeremy Brice and the Commissioner of Indiana State Police under 42 U.S.C. § 1983, claiming they conducted a warrantless search of his cell phone after his 2020 arrest on drug trafficking charges. The district court granted summary judgment in favor of the defendants based on qualified immunity, finding that no clearly established law prohibited Brice from relying on another officer's attestation that legal authority existed for the search. The Seventh Circuit affirmed, holding that neither the Supreme Court's decision in Riley v. California nor any other precedent clearly established that a forensic examiner must independently verify the validity of a warrant before searching an electronic device.

items.summary: Federal regulations prohibit public demonstrations on the Eastern Steps of the United States Capitol unless sponsored by a member of Congress. Presbyterian minister Patrick Mahoney challenged this restriction as a violation of the First Amendment, seeking to conduct prayer vigils and demonstrations on the Steps. The appellate court affirmed the district court's grant of summary judgment on the First Amendment claim but vacated the universal injunction, finding it exceeded equitable authority, and remanded for determination of appropriate relief.
items.title: Patrick Mahoney v. United States Capitol Police Board, et al

items.summary: The Copyright Royalty Board allocated cable retransmission royalties for 2014–2017 among copyright claimants using regression analysis and constant-sum surveys as equally weighted valuation methodologies. The Office of the Commissioner of Baseball and Public Broadcasting Service appealed, challenging the allocation as arbitrary and unsupported by the record. The court rejected most challenges but found the Board failed to explain how it merged the two methodologies to reach the final allocation percentages, and therefore vacated and remanded for further explanation.

items.opening_verbatim: Public Law 119–108: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to codify and extend the rules for personal casualty losses arising from major disasters and the rules for the exclusion from gross income of compensation for losses or damages
items.summary: Public Law 119–108 codifies and extends tax rules for personal casualty losses arising from major disasters declared between December 28, 2019 and January 1, 2027, effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024. The law also excludes qualified wildfire relief payments from gross income for federally declared disasters involving forest or range fires declared after December 31, 2014 and before January 1, 2027, effective for payments received in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

items.summary: S. 5438, the Alaska's Right to Produce Act 2.0, ratifies and approves all federal authorizations, permits, biological opinions, incidental take statements, and other approvals necessary for the Coastal Plain oil and gas leasing program in Alaska. The bill prohibits the President or Secretary of the Interior from placing a moratorium on or suspending oil and gas leasing in the Coastal Plain and directs federal agencies to process and maintain related authorizations. It establishes requirements for lease management unit agreements, provides exploration incentives including rental and royalty waivers, and restricts judicial review of related agency actions except through the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit.

items.summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2015-07-03, which applies to certain Cessna Aircraft Company (Cessna) (type certificate currently held by Textron Aviation, Inc.) (Textron) Model 402C and 414A airplanes. Since the FAA issued AD 2015-07-03, there have been additional reports of cracking and multi-site cracking in areas of engine beams that are difficult to access. This proposed AD would require repetitive inspections of the engine beam for cracks and applicable on-condition actions. This proposed AD would also add a new life-limit to affected engine beams and require replacement when engine beams reach this life-limit. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

items.summary: The Coast Guard is proposing to establish a temporary safety zone for a certain navigable water of Massachusetts Bay, 22 miles northeast of Boston, MA. The safety zone is needed to protect personnel, vessels, and the maritime public from potential hazards created by subsea demolition operations. This proposed rulemaking would prohibit persons and vessels from entering the safety zone unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port Sector Boston or a designated representative. We invite your comments on this proposed rulemaking.

items.summary: This interim final rule with comment period (IFC) codifies the Department of Health and Human Services' (HHS) authority to impose a temporary moratorium pausing the registration of agents and brokers that do not have a current Plan Year registration with the Federally-facilitated Exchanges at the time the moratorium is effective and are seeking to enter into Exchange agreements with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to assist consumers with enrollment through the Federally-facilitated Exchange (FFE) and State-based Exchanges that use the Federal platform (SBE-FPs) (hereinafter collectively referred to as the “Federally-facilitated Exchanges”). HHS is issuing this rule on an interim final basis. For the reasons explained in this rule, HHS finds good cause under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA) to waive prior notice and comment because providing advance notice would be contrary to the public interest and impracticable. HHS further finds good cause under the APA for this rule to become effective immediately upon publication. [official summary truncated; see source]

items.opening_verbatim: ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY 40 CFR Part 52 [EPA-R04-OAR-2025-0223; FRL-13259-01-R4] Air Plan Approval; North Carolina; Charlotte-Rock Hill Area Maintenance Plan for the 2008 8-Hour Ozone NAAQS AGENCY: Environmental Protection Agency (EP
items.summary: On February 28, 2025, the State of North Carolina, through the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality, Division of Air Quality (NCDAQ), submitted a request for the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to approve a State Implementation Plan (SIP) revision containing the State's plan for maintaining the 2008 ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS) through 2035 for the North Carolina portion of the bi-state Charlotte-Rock Hill, North Carolina-South Carolina 2008 8-hour ozone nonattainment area (the entire area is hereinafter referred to as the “bi-state Charlotte Area” and the North Carolina portion is hereinafter referred to as the “Charlotte Area”). The EPA is proposing to approve and incorporate North Carolina's second 10-year maintenance plan to maintain attainment of the 2008 8-hour ozone NAAQS in the bi-state Charlotte Area, including the 2018 and 2035 motor vehicle emission budgets (budgets) for nitrogen oxides (NO X ) and volatile organic compounds (VOC) for the Charlotte Area, into the SIP. The EPA is also notifying the public of the status of the EPA's adequacy determination for the sub-area budgets for the Charlotte Area.
items.title: Air Plan Approval; North Carolina; Charlotte-Rock Hill Area Maintenance Plan for the 2008 8-Hour Ozone NAAQS

items.summary: S. 2403 amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 to define 'adequate consideration' for valuations of closely held stock in employee stock ownership plans. The amendment permits ESOP fiduciaries to rely on valuations from independent appraisers using methodologies from Internal Revenue Service Revenue Ruling 59-60, and clarifies that this provision does not expand the Secretary of Labor's regulatory authority beyond existing scope. The amendments apply to valuations made after the bill's date of enactment.
items.title: S2403 ENR: Retire through Ownership Act

items.title: 119 S2498 RS: National Park System Long-Term Lease Investment Act

items.title: 94 S2554 RS: Alaska Native Landless Equity Act

items.summary: The bill directs the Secretary of the Interior to conduct feasibility studies on selective water withdrawal systems and alternative approaches at Glen Canyon Dam to optimize hydropower generation while preventing invasive species entrainment. The provision does not affect existing post-2026 Colorado River reservoir operations guidelines.
items.title: 90 S3743 RS: To direct the Secretary of the Interior to carry out a feasibility study on a selective water withdrawal system at Glen Canyon Dam, and for other purposes.

items.summary: The bill establishes the Water Project Navigators Program to support development and implementation of multi-benefit water projects in eligible states through grants to eligible entities for navigator positions. items.summary: H.R. 530, the ACES Act, directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to enter into an agreement with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to conduct a study on the prevalence and mortality of cancer among individuals who served as active duty aircrew in the Armed Forces. The study shall identify military occupational exposures, review literature on associations between those exposures and specific cancers, and determine prevalence and mortality rates using available data from federal agencies and the national death index. The bill also extends the deadline for pension payment limits to December 31, 2031.

FEDERAL LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER SERVICE WEAPON PURCHASE ACT OF 2025

  Mr. FRY. Mr. Speaker, pursuant to House Resolution 405, I call up the
bill (H.R. 2255) to allow Federal law enforcement officers to purchase
retired service weapons, a
items.summary: The House debated H.R. 2255, the Federal Law Enforcement Officer Service Weapon Purchase Act, which would establish a program allowing current and former federal law enforcement officers to purchase retired service weapons at salvage value from their agencies within six months of retirement. Supporters argued the measure would recover taxpayer costs and support law enforcement; opponents raised concerns about the absence of background check requirements and the scope of firearms eligible for sale.
items.title: FEDERAL LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER SERVICE WEAPON PURCHASE ACT OF 2025

items.summary: H.R. 2240 requires the Attorney General to submit three reports within 270 days on violent attacks against law enforcement officers, non-fatal aggressive incidents against officers, and mental health resources and programs available to law enforcement. items.summary: Senator Kaine moved to discharge S. Res. 195, which requests information on El Salvador's human rights practices, from the Committee on Foreign Relations. Senator Moran spoke in support of transferring administration of the Food for Peace food assistance program from USAID to the Department of Agriculture, citing the program's success in delivering American-grown commodities to hungry populations worldwide. Senator Tillis honored three North Carolina law enforcement officers killed since 2024 and urged support for the Protect and Serve Act, legislation that would make intentionally harming law enforcement officers a federal crime.
items.title: MOTION TO DISCHARGE--S. RES. 195
